scenario.description: A specialized software development team is tasked with enhancing the security and performance of an existing financial transaction processing microservice. This critical service handles high-volume, sensitive financial data, necessitating absolute precision in all security parameters and strict adherence to performance SLAs. The team consists of a Lead Architect, a Cryptography Engineer, a Performance Optimization Specialist, and a Compliance Officer. The Lead Architect oversees the overall system design and integration. The Cryptography Engineer is responsible for implementing and reviewing all encryption and data protection protocols. The Performance Optimization Specialist focuses on identifying and eliminating bottlenecks to meet latency targets. The Compliance Officer ensures that all operations adhere to financial regulations and internal security policies. A paramount, non-negotiable constraint is that all financial transaction data must be encrypted using AES-256 with a key rotation interval of exactly 29.75 days, and the service must process at least 1,000,000 transactions per hour with an end-to-end latency not exceeding 45.50 milliseconds for 99.9% of transactions. Given the extreme sensitivity and the need for constant, real-time communication on evolving threats and performance nuances, a fully connected topology is essential. This setup allows all four agents to communicate directly and instantly, ensuring that these highly precise security and performance constraints are continuously understood, meticulously implemented, and rigorously verified throughout the development and deployment phases, making this a hard structural-complexity task requiring extensive, iterative collaboration over approximately 34 turns.
